cards.title: Romanticism
cards.text: Feeling over reason. Stormy seas, wild mountains and heroic drama, often with a sense of awe at the power of nature.

cards.title: Impressionism
cards.text: Catching a passing moment of light, often painted outdoors, with quick, visible dabs of colour. Scenes of modern life and leisure.

cards.title: Post-Impressionism
cards.text: Artists who kept Impressionism's bright colour but wanted more from it: Cézanne's solid shapes, Van Gogh's swirling feeling, Seurat's tiny dots.

cards.title: How to tell them apart
cards.text: Drama and awe at nature? Romantic. A fleeting moment of light in loose dabs? Impressionist. Solid shapes, dots, patterns or swirling emotion? Post-Impressionist.

questions.q: Which painter was a Post-Impressionist, not an Impressionist?
questions.explain: Van Gogh took Impressionist colour and made it swirl with feeling.

questions.q: Which of these movements came first?
questions.explain: Romanticism was at its height in the early 1800s, decades before the Impressionists.

cards.title: Baroque
cards.text: Drama and deep shadow: strong contrasts of light and dark, powerful emotion and grand, serious subjects, often religious.

cards.title: Rococo
cards.text: Lighter and more playful: soft pastel colours, curling decoration and flirtatious scenes of love and leisure, first made fashionable in France.

cards.title: How to tell them apart
cards.text: Dark, dramatic and serious? Baroque. Light, pastel and playful? Rococo.

questions.q: Which painter was Rococo, not Baroque?
questions.explain: Fragonard painted playful, pastel scenes like The Swing.

questions.q: In which country did the Rococo style first take hold?
questions.explain: It began in Paris in the early 1700s, then spread across Europe.

cards.title: Fauvism
cards.text: Colour set free: pure, bright, unnatural colour used boldly for its own sake, led by Matisse and Derain. Les fauves means the wild beasts.

cards.title: Expressionism
cards.text: Feelings turned inside out: distorted shapes, jagged lines and harsh colour to show anxiety and inner life.

cards.title: How to tell them apart
cards.text: Both use wild colour. Joyful and decorative? Fauvist. Tense, jagged and uneasy? Expressionist.

questions.q: Which artist, with André Derain, led the Fauves?
questions.explain: Matisse and Derain were the leading figures of the group critics called the wild beasts.

questions.q: In which country was Expressionism mainly centred?
questions.explain: Groups such as Die Brücke in Dresden and Der Blaue Reiter in Munich were at its heart.
